notes:
Background: CustomerFlow Metrics runs a high-volume contact center product (outsourced + in-house). Primary focus: lower agent load via automated deflection and better summaries to speed TTR. Ops team extremely cost-sensitive — current infra spends ~ $120k/mo on embeddings+generation across multiple vendors.

Recent conversations:
- 2025-01-15 intro: CEO says 'need predictable unit costs; spikes kill margins' — good buy-in from product.
- 2025-02-02 tech deep-dive w/ SRE+ML: heavy interest in batching/caching and quantization to reduce tokens/infer cost. Wants measurable unit economics per 1k sessions.
- 2025-02-20 pricing + security call (Fireflies ff_20250220_8342): asked for dedicated capacity options and fallbacks to smaller quantized models during peak windows.

Requirements summary (from product + infra):
- Workloads: real-time chat deflection (primary), agent assist (secondary), nightly summarization for tickets, tool calling for CRM updates.
- Volume: baseline 3M user messages/mo; peaks up to 9M during promos.
- Latency SLOs: p50 <200ms for model response in live chat; p95 <800ms.
- Throughput: sustain bursts of 250 RPS for 5-10 minute windows.
- Cost target: reduce current per-message AI cost by 40% vs current vendors; ARR-friendly pricing.
- Model preferences: open model family preferred, with vendor-managed quantized variants; ability to pin model versions and route to cheaper variants during spikes.
- Routing/fallback: must support policy-based routing (latency vs cost), automatic fallback to quantized model or cached reply.
- Data/security: VPC, SOC2 required, KMS for keys, audit logs for every inference, retention controls, EU residency for EU customer data.

POC ask: 8-week bench + staged POC to simulate production traffic at 3x to 5x baseline. Deliverables: latency/cost dashboards, sample rollout policy, integration with their CRM tool-calling hooks, and a short runbook for spike behavior.

Sales notes / personality:
- Buying group: Head of Product (champion), VP Ops (cost owner), Head of Security (gatekeeper), Procurement.
- Pain: unpredictable token costs during spikes, noisy billing across multiple vendors, and poor reliability when load increases.
- Quote from Head of Product: 'We need to know what a peak week will cost us before it happens.'

Concise POC concerns flagged by SE:
- Data residency test (EU) must be included in POC; otherwise security will stop demo.
- Need a clear rollback plan; cannot risk customer-facing failures during promo spikes.
- Integration complexity for tool-calling (CRM API) — they require example adaptor code.

Stated blockers and next steps:
- Blockers: security KMS policy, legal needs DPA + data residency appendix, internal budget window > Mar 2025.
- Next steps: deliver POC SOW + cost model by 2025-03-06; schedule engineering kickoff and load-test plan week of 2025-03-10.

CRM notes tone: compact, lots of fragments, copies of key quotes and ask items. Keep follow-up cadence tight (weekly).
